As an IT Specialist (System Analysis) "Product Manager", GS-2210-14, you will be responsible for: Leading the development of FSA products by understanding the needs of students, families, and stakeholders, translating insights into product roadmaps, prioritizing high-impact features, and measuring success by user outcomes.

Serving as the bridge between policy goals, technical systems, and user needs by translating complex constraints into actionable requirements and ensuring compliant, secure, and user-friendly solutions at national scale.

Collaborating and aligning with contractors, partner agencies, and cross-functional teams to align efforts with the product vision, hold vendors accountable for outcomes, and deliver tangible improvements for users.

Fostering a product culture of experimentation, data-driven decision-making, and continuous improvement while providing vision and expert recommendations that align government staff and vendors around shared goals for students and families.

Experience serving as a product manager, overseeing internal and external software development, testing, integration, and operation. Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and translating business requirements into technical user stories.

Knowledge of product management principles, with a focus on user-centered design and measurable outcomes. Skill in managing vendors and cross-functional teams to deliver results and drive tangible product improvements.

Ability to inspire and sustain a mission-driven product culture and drive collaborative efforts amongst the teams. Knowledge of building and operating large-scale, mission-critical systems or comparable technology infrastructure.

Was wir suchen
Jedes Unternehmen braucht laufend neue Kunden – und genau dieses Problem lösen wir. Mit Interlead bauen die #1 Plattform für Leads, Termine und Aufträge und machen die Kundengewinnung für unsere Partner damit einfacher, transparenter und planbarer.
Zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt suchen wir daher einen Product Owner (m/w/d) für unser Tech Team (hybrid/remote).
Das sind deine Aufgaben
Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung unserer Lead-Matching-Software – unserer eigens entwickelten Kernanwendung zur automatisierten Neukundengewinnung.
Du sorgst dafür, dass die Entwicklung reibungslos voranschreitet und unsere Entwickler jederzeit an den richtigen Prioritäten arbeiten.
Du konzipierst eigenständig neue Features, nimmst Anforderungen aus den Fachabteilungen und von Usern auf und übersetzt sie in klare Arbeitspakete (z. B. Tickets, Mockups etc.).
Du prüfst neue Features auf Funktionalität und Qualität, begleitest den Release-Prozess und verantwortest den Live-Gang.
Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen I T, Fachabteilungen und externen Dienstleistern und sorgst während des gesamten Entwicklungsprozesses für eine transparente Kommunikation.
Du hältst alle relevanten Stakeholder regelmäßig über den aktuellen Entwicklungsstand auf dem Laufenden.
Du identifizierst, konzipierst und implementierst AI-Anwendungen , die unsere Softwarelösungen und internen Prozesse intelligenter und effizienter machen – von der ersten Idee bis zum produktiven Einsatz.
Dank deiner Expertise erreichst du folgende Meilensteine bei uns

Du lernst die Leadbase (Matching, Dialer, Partner-Portal, Versand & Abrechnung sowie APIs) und die wichtigsten Stakeholder aus Vertrieb, Operations und Tech kennen.
Du übernimmst die Pflege des Backlogs sowie die laufende Priorisierung der Tickets im Tech-Team.
Du setzt erste kleinere Verbesserungen eigenständig um – von der Anforderungsaufnahme über die Qualitätssicherung bis zum Live-Gang.
Du etablierst regelmäßige Kommunikationsformate (z. B. wöchentliche Status-Updates oder Release Notes) und hältst Fachabteilungen sowie Management über den Entwicklungsstand auf dem Laufenden.

Du verantwortest eigenständig ein größeres Feature oder eine Produktinitiative der Leadbase – von der Konzeption bis zum erfolgreichen Rollout.
Du stehst im regelmäßigen Austausch mit den Fachbereichen und priorisierst Anforderungen nach ihrem Nutzen und ihrer Relevanz.
Du identifizierst konkrete Einsatzmöglichkeiten für KI und setzt erste Prozessoptimierungen um (z. B. zur Automatisierung von Anforderungsprozessen oder zur Steigerung der internen Produktivität).

Du gestaltest die Produktstrategie für Lead Matching und angrenzende Module (z. B. Dialer, Multi-Channel und Partner-API) aktiv mit und bringst mindestens ein strategisches Vorhaben erfolgreich in Produktion.
Du hast mindestens eine KI-Lösung erfolgreich produktiv eingeführt.
Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Produktfragen rund um die Leadbase und wirst von Fachabteilungen sowie externen Partnern als verlässliche Schnittstelle wahrgenommen.
Das bringst du mit
Du bringst Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager in einem agilen Umfeld mit – idealerweise in einem SaaS- oder Tech-Unternehmen.
Du verfügst über ein gutes technisches Verständnis und hast Freude daran, die Brücke zwischen Business und Entwicklung zu schlagen.
Du hast erste Berührungspunkte mit künstlicher Intelligenz oder ein fundiertes Interesse daran, KI-Lösungen praxisnah im Unternehmenskontext einzusetzen.
Du arbeitest strukturiert und proaktiv und kannst komplexe Anforderungen in klare Aufgaben und Prioritäten übersetzen.
Du kommunizierst sicher und verständlich – auch bei technischen Themen und mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern.
Du begeisterst dich für datengetriebene, digitale Produkte und hast den Anspruch, Dinge aktiv voranzubringen und nachhaltig zu verbessern.
Das bieten wir dir
Ein dynamisches Marketing- und Tech-Umfeld sowie die Möglichkeit, gemeinsam “The Lead Company” aufzubauen.
Ein riesiger Markt und zahlreiche interne Wachstumsmöglichkeiten – wir lösen das größte Problem unserer Partner: die Automatisierung ihrer Neukundengewinnung.
Volle Flexibilität im Arbeitsort (remote, im Bremer Headquarter oder nach Absprache auch aus dem Ausland).
Volle Flexibilität in der Arbeitszeit – du gestaltest deine Arbeitszeiten individuell mit deinem Team.
30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr + die Möglichkeit, jederzeit unbezahlten Urlaub zu nehmen.
Zuschuss zur betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (die “Interlead‑Rente”).
Jährliche Teamevents wie Sommerfest & Weihnachtsfeier.
Agiles Arbeitsumfeld – moderne Tools wie Slack, Monday, Notion, Google Workspace und OKRs/Scrum unterstützen dich bei der täglichen Arbeit.
Zuschuss fürs Fitnessstudio (über Urban Sports Club oder E‑Gym Wellpass).
Schnelle Entscheidungen – wir sind 100 % bootstrapped, profitabel und unabhängig von Investoren.
Eine offene Feedback‑Kultur und regelmäßige interne Trainings.
Transparente Kommunikation durch monatliche All‑Hands‑Meetings , wöchentlichen Newsletter und feste Team‑Updates.
Im Headquarter in der Bremer Überseestadt erwarten dich ergonomische Arbeitsplätze, großartiger Kaffee & Espresso, Getränke und Grillabende.
Für Home‑Office‑Mitarbeitende: monatliche Home‑Office‑Pauschale von 20 €.
Bikeleasing, lease dein Wunschfahrrad oder E-Bike zu attraktiven Konditionen.
Das sind unsere Werte
Fail Fast: Wir leben eine ausgeprägte Testing- und Fehlerkultur. Wir sind pragmatisch, mutig und fühlen uns mit Veränderung wohl.
Ergebnisse: Wir arbeiten flexibel, aber verlässlich. Bei uns steht Freiheit in Einklang mit Ergebnisorientierung und Eigenverantwortung.
Vertrauen: Wir gehen offen mit Zahlen, Stärken und Schwächen um und machen das, was für die Firma richtig ist ("Ego zurück").

s.t:
Was haben ein Top-Mountainbike, ein künstliches Hüftgelenk und ein Smartphone gemeinsam? Wir entwickeln die Software, um diese High-End-Produkte herzustellen! Mit hyperMILL® steuern wir CNC-Maschinen und haben höchste Ansprüche an Leistung und Teilequalität.
Wir sind einer der weltweit führenden Entwickler von leistungsstarken CAD/CAM-Lösungen – und das seit mehr als 30 Jahren! Unsere innovativen CAD/CAM-Technologien sorgen für eine deutlich höhere Performance im Programmierprozess und setzen internationale Maßstäbe in der zerspanenden Fertigung.
Für unser Produktmanagement suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt einen erfahrenen Produktmanager (m/w/d) mit starkem Verständnis für zerspanende Prozesse und der 2.5D, 3-Achs und 5-Achs-Bearbeitung.
Ihre Tätigkeitsschwerpunkte
Identifikation, Priorisierung und Validierung von Kundenanforderungen, Marktpotenzialen und technologischen Chancen im Bereich 2.5D-, 3-Achs- und 5-Achs-Bearbeitung
Begleitung der Produktentwicklung von der Problemdefinition und Discovery über die Konzeption bis zur erfolgreichen Markteinführung neuer Funktionen und Lösungen
Bewertung von Anforderungen hinsichtlich Kundennutzen, technischer Machbarkeit und strategischer Relevanz sowie aktive Mitgestaltung der Produktstrategie
Absicherung neuer Konzepte und Lösungen durch Kundenfeedback, Praxistests sowie strukturierte Risikoanalysen
Zusammenarbeit mit Entwicklung, QA, Anwendungstechnik, Support, Marketing und Vertrieb zur Sicherstellung einer konsistenten und erfolgreichen Produktentwicklung

Sicherstellung der konsistenten Integration neuer Funktionen in Bezug auf User Experience, Produktstrategie und hyperMILL-Gesamtkonzept sowie Verantwortung für die Erreichung definierter Produktziele und die nachhaltige Verbesserung des Kundennutzens
Ihr Profil
Tiefgreifendes Wissen in der Zerspanung sowie fundiertes Verständnis von CAM-Prozessen, CNC-Maschinen, Steuerungen, Werkzeugen und Fertigungsabläufen
Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im CAM-, Zerspanungs- oder Produktmanagementumfeld sowie Erfahrung in der Entwicklung, Validierung und Markteinführung technischer Produktlösungen
Souveräne Bewertung von Anforderungen, Risiken und Prioritäten sowie Fähigkeit zur verständlichen Aufbereitung komplexer technischer Sachverhalte
Sicheres Agieren im Austausch mit Kunden sowie interdisziplinären Teams und Stakeholdern

📍 Standort: Berlin (hybrid)
🕓 Start: Ab sofort | Vollzeit | unbefristet
Als Product Manager (m/w/d) verantwortest Du die Weiterentwicklung unserer SaaS-Lösung für die Immobilienverwaltung (App & Plattform) in Deutschland. Du setzt die richtigen Prioritäten, arbeitest eng mit unseren Teams in Deutschland und Paris zusammen und bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für den deutschen Markt.

Du entwickelst die Produktvision und -strategie für Deutschland auf Basis von Daten, Markt- und Wettbewerbsanalysen
Du priorisierst und verantwortest die Produkt-Roadmap in enger Abstimmung mit den deutschen Teams
Du setzt Roadmap-Themen gemeinsam mit Tech, Design, GenAI und Operations um

Du koordinierst Releases, Kommunikation und Abstimmung mit den Fachbereichen

s.t:
Du lebst in Berlin und arbeitest gerne regelmäßig im Büro mit den Teams
Du hast 1–4 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktmanagement, idealerweise im Start-up-Umfeld
Du nutzt KI selbstverständlich in Deinem PM-Alltag für Analyse, Automatisierung und Prototyping
Du fühlst Dich in einem schnellen, dynamischen Umfeld wohl und treibst Themen eigenständig voran
Du arbeitest strukturiert, kommunizierst klar und kollaborierst teamübergreifend
Bei Matera garantieren wir Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Hier bist du so willkommen, wie du bist!

Vergütung: 55.000–75.000 € brutto pro Jahr , abhängig von Deiner Erfahrung.
Matera Benefits wie vergünstigte Urban Sports Club Mitgliedschaft, Lunch-Gutscheine + monatlicher ÖPNV-Zuschuss
Einen großen Verantwortungsbereich und echte Gestaltungsfreiheit ab dem ersten Tag: Du bist der Product Manager für das deutsche Produkt und hast maßgeblichen Einfluss auf dessen Entwicklung.
Ein Umfeld, in dem Du schnell lernst: Ein erfahrenes französisches Product-Team unterstützt Dich, gleichzeitig arbeitest Du direkt mit dem Country Manager und den operativen Teams zusammen.
Ein profitables, stark wachsendes Unternehmen mit einer klaren europäischen Vision.
Ein Büro in Berlin mit mindestens drei Präsenztagen pro Woche sowie gelegentlichen Reisen nach Paris, um Zeit mit dem Product- und Tech-Team zu verbringen.
Ein ambitioniertes Team mit starkem Zusammenhalt und Spaß an der Arbeit 🙂

Unsere Mission bei Matera ist es, Wohnungseigentümer*innen glücklich zu machen! Durch uns können sie ihre Immobilie transparent und einfach selbst verwalten, oder die Verwaltung ganzheitlich in unsere Hände legen und dadurch eine Menge Zeit und Geld sparen.

Seit 2017 sind wir auf dem französischen Markt aktiv und machen bereits jeden Tag das Leben von mehr als 100.000 Wohnungseigentümer*innen besser. In Deutschland haben wir seit 2021 ebenfalls einen großartigen Start mit einem ambitionierten Team hingelegt.
Um unser Team kennenzulernen und Eindrücke von unserer Kultur zu bekommen, schaue gerne bei uns auf LinkedIn oder auf Instagram vorbei!

About Remote Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams.

With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remote rs working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.

With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role. We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.

If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! What this job can offer you This is an exciting time to join Remote and make a personal difference in the global employment space as a Product Manager , joining our Product team in the Fintech vertical .

As a Billing Platform Product Manager, you will be a key member of our triad of product managers in the billing team, each leading their independent teams yet working within an interconnected scope. As a Product Manager at Remote , you'll be developing and guiding our strategy for a key product area in Finance.

You'll advance this vision by working with a cross-functional engineering and design group to find our most important problems and shape iterative solutions towards them. What you bring Prior experience as product manager in billing / invoicing or similar, ideally at a high-growth company Proficiency in Cursor and/or Claude Code or similar tool.

You must be able to autonomously build, debug, and ship functional prototypes or small code changes with the help of AI tooling, not just write specs.

Great judgment making both strategic (what to prioritize) and tactical (feature scope) decisions Demonstrable, self-driven results that have moved a product in the right direction A passion for creating seamless and effective products, even when the challenges they address are complex and intricate.

Outstanding communication and collaboration skills, including across different departments (e.g. business operations, sales, etc.) to ensure that we’re satisfying critical business requirements Proficient in English, both written and spoken. Bonus: Experience working in a remote environment.

Key Responsibilities Build solutions together with the rest of the team that solve for finance, billing and other financial services at Remote Own not just software implementation, but the end-to-end experience: Remote delivers value through services powered by both humans and software Lead on complex solutions without requiring support or involvement from senior members of the product team Effectively manage internal expectations for complex projects, products, and features while navigating challenging prioritization decisions Drive Remote in the right direction by building an effective roadmap and strategy for your area of the product in Finance Break down strategic plans into near and mid-term goals that's easy for others to understand Align your product roadmap with higher level department and company problems we’re working to solve Be the subject matter expert for your product area Contribute to scaling and growth plans for your product area Ship improvements quickly and iteratively, challenging yourself and counterparts to find minimal solutions to problems Support and leads a product team delivering high throughput and high return on investment Understand key business KPIs and align your team's work and metrics to directly improve to these Work together with engineers, designers and stakeholders to build solutions to important complex problems Communicate and collaborate internally and externally Contribute to the Product org by sharing your techniques, processes, and learnings Communicate and promote the work of your team and why it matters to customers and internal teams Work asynchronously and transparently Lead on solutions with minimal support or involvement from senior members of the product team.

You should be able to work autonomously on simple features and iterations, only needing support to solve complex problems Contribute to tactical and strategic decision-making for your business area Develop into a subject matter expert for understanding, articulating, and solving complex business problems related to our mobile experiences Practicals You'll report to: Group Product Manager Location : For this position we welcome everyone to apply Start date: As soon as possible Remote Compensation Philosophy Remote 's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate.

We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries. At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context.

At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally. The base salary range for this full-time position is $62,400 to $140,400.

Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands.

The base salary range may be subject to change. At Remote , we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness.

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.

You are equally comfortable prototyping alongside engineering as you are presenting a product strategy to internal and external executives. You do not separate strategy from execution — you own both, and you move fluidly between them. What you will own:

As part of this role, you will identify new business opportunities and win clients for ARISE. You are passionate about developing customer relationships, thrive on opening new doors, and have the tenacity and resilience to turn prospects into long-term clients.

This role is designed to be actively shaped and driven by the person in it. While the near-term focus is strongly centered on delivery, execution, and stabilising platform-level coherence under ongoing pressure, you are expected to deliberately push the role and the platform toward a more outcome-driven footing. You will take end-to-end ownership for platform-level coherence across multiple product lines , balancing short-term delivery demands with the long-term evolution of the platform toward usability, operability, and cost efficiency.
You will represent Platform Operations as a primary customer persona and act as their main interface into product management , shaping the end-to-end operational journey of the platform and translating operational, reliability, and cost-related needs into clear and actionable product priorities.

You will actively surface, resolve, and de-risk cross-product dependencies by identifying unknowns early, unblocking teams, and ensuring consistent platform behavior and correct sequencing across planning and delivery. You will drive new business by identifying, engaging, and winning new clients while building long-term customer relationships that support ARISE's continued growth.

The Opportunity
As Product Manager - Merchant Experience, you will own the discovery, definition, and delivery of Xplor 's self-serve merchant portal: the place where merchants see their transactions and payouts, understand their fees, pull reports, and manage their account.

It is the everyday face of Xplor 's payments platform, and your job is to make it clear, trustworthy, and genuinely useful across global markets. This portal also acts as the internal platform our own teams use to support and configure those merchants.
You will sit at the intersection of product craft, payments, and data - turning information owned by the billing, payout, and financials teams into an experience that answers a merchant's most important questions at a glance: have I been paid, what did it cost me, and is my account set up the way I need? You will partner closely with design and research, and with the upstream teams whose data you surface.

Merchant Portal Strategy & Roadmap
Own and evolve the strategy and roadmap for Xplor 's self-serve merchant portal across global markets.
Define a vision for a merchant experience that is clear, trustworthy, and reduces the need to contact support.
Prioritise ruthlessly against merchant impact, adoption, and support deflection, and present priorities to the VP of Product.
Align your roadmap with the billing, payout, and financials teams whose data the portal surfaces.
Transactions, Payouts & Reporting
Own the surfaces where merchants view transactions and payouts.
Define clear, accurate reporting and statements that merchants can pull themselves, without raising a ticket.
Make fees and deductions transparent, so merchants understand their cost of payments.
Ensure the money shown to merchants is accurate and reconciled with the underlying platform data.
Account Management & Self-Serve
Own merchant self-service: managing account details, users and permissions, and settings without contacting support.
Identify the highest-volume support reasons that the portal should be able to deflect, and design self-serve flows to remove them.
Build in-product help and guidance that meets merchants where they are.
Track and reduce support contact rates for portal-addressable issues as a core metric.
Merchant Configuration & Enablement
Own the configuration portal the BMS team uses to set up and maintain merchants: pricing, fees, product configuration, and account settings.
Own and drive the capabilities of our configuration portal to remove work out of engineering and into the hands of the team closest to the merchant, with the guardrails that money-affecting changes require.
Define validation, approvals, and change history for pricing and fee changes, so a mistake is hard to make and easy to trace.
Work with the billing, payout, and financials teams to make sure configuration set internally is reflected accurately in what the merchant sees and is charged.
Experience, Craft & Adoption
Partner closely with design and engineering to ship intuitive, well-crafted experiences grounded in real merchant needs.
Run discovery with merchants to understand their jobs-to-be-done and validate solutions before building.
Use product analytics to understand behaviour, find friction, and measure the impact of what you ship.
Drive adoption and engagement of the portal, improving task success and merchant satisfaction over time.
AI-Augmented Product Practice
Embed AI tools into every stage of the product lifecycle: use LLMs for rapid synthesis of merchant interviews and support-ticket themes, competitor teardowns, and PRD first drafts; use AI assistants to prototype portal flows and copy without full engineering overhead.
Champion AI adoption across the product team - document effective prompting patterns, share workflows, and upskill peers.
Use AI-powered analytics to surface friction and anomalies in portal usage data and generate plain-language summaries for stakeholders.
Stay current with the evolving AI tooling landscape relevant to product management, operating at a higher output cadence than a traditional PM.
Delivery & Stakeholder Management
Drive agile delivery with engineering, design, and data using clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Manage dependencies with the billing, payout, financials, and data teams whose information the portal surfaces.
Coordinate with support and partner teams to make sure the portal reflects what merchants actually need.
Monitor product health via metrics such as adoption, task success, support deflection, and merchant satisfaction.
Required
3-4 years of product management experience, with at least 2 years building B2B SaaS, dashboard, portal, or self-serve products.
Strong product craft: discovery, design partnership, and a track record of shipping intuitive self-serve experiences.
Experience presenting complex or financial data clearly to non-technical users (for example transactions, payouts, or reporting).
A track record of improving adoption, engagement, or support-deflection metrics.
Comfort working with product analytics to understand behaviour and measure impact.
Enough payments literacy to represent transactions, payouts, and fees accurately, or the ability to ramp on this quickly.
Excellent written and verbal communication and strong partnership with design and research.
Hands-on proficiency with AI productivity tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or equivalent) with demonstrable examples of using AI to increase PM output and quality.
Comfortable working in a globally distributed team across time zones from an India base.

Experience with merchant, seller, or customer-facing financial dashboards.
Familiarity with payments concepts: settlement, payouts, fees, and statements.
Background in embedded payments, fintech, or vertical SaaS.
Experience with self-serve support deflection and in-product help or guidance.
Familiarity with design systems and accessibility standards.
Experience building a unified experience on top of data owned by multiple upstream teams.

About Netholabs
Netholabs builds large-scale neural and behavioural recording platforms to generate the data needed for the next generation of brain models. We operate two recording platforms: a preclinical ethological monitoring system integrated with behaviour and neural data and a human motion-capture and neurophysiology platform. We are a small, fast-moving team where hardware, neuroscience, and ML sit in the same room.

We are building integrated human motion-capture and neurophysiological recording systems for both controlled lab studies and naturalistic, in-the-wild data collection. Today we have working prototypes. We need someone to turn them into products - reproducible, manufacturable, remotely updatable systems that can be deployed at scale and maintained without an engineer in the room.
You will own R&D delivery across the London lab and hardware programme: co-developing the hardware with our electronics and mechanical engineers, importing and enforcing best-practice data capture protocols, and engaging contract manufacturers to scale. This is an agentic, hands-on role -with support engineer roles as required. You will spend as much time in the lab and on the phone with suppliers as you will in a spec document.

Take working prototypes to shippable, field-deployable systems — define the product, own the roadmap, and drive it to delivery
Specify and build out over-the-air update infrastructure: firmware, versioning, rollback, fleet management, remote diagnostics
Own the design-for-manufacture transition — DFM/DFA reviews, BOM ownership, tolerancing, test fixtures, and production test protocols
Identify, qualify, and manage contract manufacturers and suppliers; own the relationship from RFQ through NPI to sustained production
Establish and enforce best-practice data capture protocols across modalities (EEG, fNIRS, EMG, pupillometry, motion capture, video) so that data quality is consistent across sessions, operators, and sites
Define the requirements that make in-the-wild collection viable: wearability, session setup time, robustness, battery life, and unattended operation
Work directly with our electronics, mechanical, firmware, and neuroscience teams to translate research needs into hardware requirements — and push back when a requirement doesn't survive contact with manufacturing
Build the quality, documentation, and regulatory groundwork (design history, ISO 13485-style discipline, CE/UKCA pathway) appropriate to a research-device product
Contribute to the industrialisation of our rodent recording platform where the manufacturing and OTA problems overlap

Essential
Min 3+ years (ideal 7+) in hardware product management, product engineering, or programme management, with several products you personally took from prototype to volume manufacture
Direct, demonstrable experience with contract manufacturers: you have run RFQs, sat through NPI builds, argued about yield, and fixed a production line problem from 6,000 miles away
Deep understanding of connected-device architecture: OTA update mechanisms, device provisioning, telemetry, fleet management, and what it costs to get these wrong
Fluency across electronics, mechanical, and firmware enough to hold a real technical conversation with each - you don't need to design the board, but you need to know when the answer you're getting is wrong
Track record of writing specifications and protocols that people actually follow
Comfort with ambiguity and a small-company reality: no PMO, no roadmap tooling team, no one to delegate the boring parts to

Experience with wearable, biosignal, or medical device hardware
Familiarity with human research data collection — protocols, participant handling, IRB/ethics, GDPR and special-category data
Experience shipping a product to CE/UKCA or FDA pathway
Background in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, or a related field
Experience with multi-sensor time synchronisation and the data infrastructure behind it

Direct ownership of a product line at a company small enough that your decisions ship
Equity in an early-stage company building foundational infrastructure for brain modelling
A team of neuroscientists and engineers doing genuinely novel work
Central London lab, on-site, with access to the Sussex rodent facility

OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Singapore, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.
Who We Are
At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me , Do the Right Thing , and Get Things Done . These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.
About The Opportunity
OKX is expanding its presence across Latin America, and we're looking for a locally embedded Product Manager to drive market growth in the region. This role sits at the intersection of local market strategy and product execution — you'll identify business and product opportunities unique to LatAm, shape how we localize the trading experience, and own the end-to-end user trading journey for the region.
This is not a "translate and ship" role. We need someone who deeply understands how LatAm users discover, onboard, trade, and grow — and who can turn that understanding into product decisions that move our regional metrics.
What You’ll Be Doing
Local Market Opportunity & Strategy
Identify and prioritize business and product opportunities specific to Latin American markets, including regional payment rails, local trading behaviors, regulatory nuances, and competitive gaps.
Build and maintain a deep understanding of the LatAm crypto and fintech landscape — including key competitors, user segments, regulatory trends, and macro factors that influence trading adoption.
Develop go-to-market product strategies tailored to LatAm user segments (e.g., first-time crypto users, active retail traders, remittance-driven users).
Partner with regional BD, marketing, and operations teams to align product initiatives with local growth objectives.
User Trading Journey Ownership
Own and optimize the full user trading journey across APP and WEB — from discovery and onboarding (Markets, Chart analysis) through execution (Order placement, Chart trading, Position management) to post-trade review (Asset analysis, Trading journal).
Define and execute the product roadmap for trading experience improvements in the region, balancing global platform capabilities with local user needs.
Analyze user behavior, funnel data, and feedback specific to LatAm markets to identify pain points and high-impact opportunities for conversion, retention, and engagement.
Develop strategies to serve diverse user profiles — from advanced traders to speculative and novice traders — adapting the product to their distinct preferences and requirements.
Cross-functional Collaboration
Work closely with Design, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to translate user insights into shipped product features and iterative improvements.
Collaborate with UX/UI designers to optimize trading interface layout and usability, ensuring a seamless and intuitive experience.
Partner with Engineering to ensure efficient feature implementation, maintaining a balance between innovation and operational feasibility.
Measure the impact of product initiatives through well-defined metrics, using data-driven insights to refine strategies and deliver measurable outcomes.
What We Look For In You
5+ years of product management experience with a demonstrated track record in consumer-facing product, ideally in trading, fintech, or crypto.
Solid understanding of manual trading workflows across mobile and web — including the needs and behaviors of different trader personas.
Strong ability to translate user research and local market insights into actionable product roadmaps.
Excellent product sense, attention to detail, and a history of shipping products that users love.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable working with data to prioritize, validate hypotheses, and measure outcomes.
Proven cross-functional leadership — able to align design, engineering, data, and commercial teams around a shared vision.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Nice-To-Haves
Proficiency in Spanish and/or Portuguese. Candidates who can engage with LatAm users and stakeholders in local languages will have a strong advantage, though this is not a strict requirement.
Direct experience in the Latin American market — understanding of local user behaviors, payment ecosystems, regulatory environments, and cultural nuances across the region.
Hands-on trading experience in FX, stocks, or crypto.
Familiarity with technical analysis tools and charting platforms.
Experience working in globally distributed teams with cross-regional collaboration.

Following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.
We are looking for a Lead Technical Product Manager to join our Supply domain , more specifically in the Rail Integrations team, which is responsible for onboarding carriers onto our system (integrating external systems and harmonising data structures). Lead and grow a team of Technical Product Managers and Integration Analysts, setting the standard for technical excellence and ownership.

Turn integration into a competitive advantage by driving automation, slashing time-to-live, and building scalable infrastructure no competitor can match.
Own the roadmap end-to-end — make the tough prioritisation calls and deliver features that directly grow inventory and revenue.

Experience scoping and delivering B2B integrations with external partners or enterprise clients, managing complexity across technical, commercial, and operational dimensions.

We have strong foundations. But to reach more markets, more brands, and more patients, we need a growth platform that gives us capabilities we don't yet have.
This isn't about what to build on the surface. It's about what foundational capabilities unlock the next step change — in conversion, retention, and how fast a new market can go live. Sometimes that's personalisation. Sometimes authentication. Sometimes embedding AI into exactly the right moment in the patient journey. You'll figure that out, own the roadmap, and ship it. The roadmap doesn't exist yet — you'll define it.
You'll work with a cross-functional squad of engineers and designers and:
Define and own the growth platform strategy and roadmap — the foundational capabilities that unlock conversion, activation, retention, and market scalability
Translate platform investments into business outcomes — every capability has a clear hypothesis for how it moves a growth metric, shipped incrementally and not after a six-month build
Embed AI where it genuinely improves outcomes — identifying the moments where an intelligent layer makes the experience materially better
Enable dynamic experiences across landing pages, onboarding, and in-product surfaces — the CMS, feature flagging, and content infrastructure that lets teams move without engineering dependency
Build a tech stack that launches a new market in weeks, not months
This is a platform role, not an infrastructure role. You care about what the platform enables for patients and growth teams — and you ship incrementally to prove it.

You're a product manager who's comfortable in the space between user experience and engineering infrastructure. You think in systems and capabilities — but you never lose sight of the patient on the other end, or the growth team trying to move a metric.
You don't treat platform work as a reason to slow down. You know how to slice a large capability into meaningful increments that ship value fast, and you hold yourself accountable to growth metrics even when the work lives under the surface.
Solid PM experience with meaningful time on platform, growth, data, or infrastructure
You hold the technical and commercial view at once — you know what's being built, why it matters to the patient, and how it moves a metric
Comfortable with ambiguity — you can take "we need to be better at personalisation" and turn it into a sequenced, defensible roadmap without waiting to be told what to build
Adaptable — requirements change and you move with them, without losing sight of where you're going
Comfortable working with data teams — event tracking, user identity, and data models aren't foreign to you
Strong cross-functional instincts — you build alignment across engineering, data, design, and growth without needing authority
Genuinely curious about where AI actually belongs in a product experience
Bonus points for healthcare experience, multi-market platform thinking, or building personalisation engines.

Make real impact, fast - We build in the open together, which helps us learn and iterate more quickly to deliver high-quality outcomes faster than anyone else. Helping impact patients’ lives for the better from the moment you join Euc.
Location flexibility: You can choose to work hybrid in Berlin or relocate to London, UK (we will pay for sponsorship!)
You’ll be supported to accelerate your career - Regular feedback alongside our bi-annual performance reviews, a professional development budget & leave help ensure you have the support you need to level up. We’re committed to helping every Eucalypt reach their full potential.
You’ll work with others who are incredibly passionate about what they do - Our talent bar is high, and our work ethic is strong. You’ll get to stretch yourself every day, be given autonomy to tackle interesting problems, and work amongst people who care deeply about our patients.

About Manifest
Manifest is building modern software for the tours and activities industry.
Our customers run real-world businesses: tours, attractions, experiences, rentals, and activities. They need software that helps them sell more, operate smoothly, and deliver great guest experiences.
We're building a B2B2C SaaS platform that brings booking, ecommerce, payments, accounting, operations, and customer experience together in a modern architecture. The product surface is broad, the workflows are nuanced, and the opportunity is big.

That surface now spans several distinct product areas, including a newer, AI-native platform for building and delivering customer websites end-to-end. This is not a backlog management role. We're looking for someone who can take ambiguous customer and business problems, find the shape of the opportunity, make smart tradeoffs, and help a cross-functional team ship high-quality product experiences.

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll turn customer insight, business context, and technical possibilities into clear product direction and own the delivery end-to-end.
Modern product work is changing, and this role reflects that. You do not need to be a front-end engineer, and you won't be expected to write production code. Product Manager - Limbic Access
Limbic builds AI-powered mental healthcare. Our front-door Access product talks to thousands of patients a month across the NHS and major US health systems. Access is past 0→1 in the UK and US: the product exists, customers are live, the model is proven. We're hiring a Product Manager to take it 1→10 in the US, against a growing pipeline of enterprise customers, owning the team's day-to-day product cadence. The job is to ship and ship well.
What You'll Own
You'll own the week-to-week rhythm that turns engineering into shipped product:
Run the team's ceremonies: effective, alignment-creating, always followed up on.
Own roadmap prioritisation. Understand the projects in play, weigh their relative impact, and sequence them. Ground the sequencing in customer signal, and user feedback, usage, and behaviour.
Triage the inbound: bugs, debt, CS asks, scope additions. Separate real issues from noise, route to the right owner, decide what gets iterated when.
Scope and define the work. Write project overviews the team can act on, ensuring the next-highest-value project is always lined up.
Own the incident loop. Triage, root cause, fix, follow-up. Engineers get space to fix; you hold the loop.
Keep the product well instrumented. Mixpanel today and whatever's next. Ensure the team can answer its own questions from the data, and that you can read user behavior out of it.
Protect engineering focus. Hold the line on scope creep from any sources. Check in 1:1 mid-cycle with anyone who's blocked or drifting.

You've shipped product before. Maybe one or two roles in. You want real product management. The kind where you own outcomes, not Jira tickets.
You ship features and projects that move metrics and create outcomes. Not work that's about looking good.
Comfortable with engineers and engineering concepts. You build strong mental models for how products work and apply them in your day-to-day.
You write clearly and quickly. You think clearly from first principles.
You think critically with data. You can pull insights yourself, interrogate how they were generated, and reason about what they actually mean. Not 'I made a decision with data once.'
You never produce AI slop, but you do heavily rely on AI in your day-to-day. You go beyond using AI to write PRDs.
You are 'client safe' - you can represent Limbic to customers professionally.
You can say no to someone and make them feel it's in their best interest.
You build products. You know the difference between a feature that creates repeatable value and a one-off that introduces drag and tech debt.
Healthcare experience is a bonus, but not a requirement. EHR integration and working knowledge of health-data standards (HL7, FHIR) especially.
You won't fit if you need polished process, a heavy spec phase, or a team that loves meetings. We're ahead of our process.
Why This Role
Two things to know.
One. It's a delivery role for now, with a clear set of projects to execute on (but prioritize and sequence effectively). You'll grow into more strategic scope over the next 4-6 months. The immediate brief is to make the engineering team's product cadence quieter and more predictable.
Two. The team is small and load is high. The hire exists because we need to free senior product time for discovery and strategy on a separate product. You might feel the pressure of that. In return: real customers (millions of lives) and the opportunity to iterate the product in a company-defining direction.

Why Mozilla ?
Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser.

Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more.

And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.
The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

This role owns the foundation that lets other software drive Firefox: the secure, reliable connection an outside tool or another team uses to act inside the browser, and the building blocks they call to do it. It enables the teams building on it — internal teams, outside AI tools — to create their own products on top. This role owns the shared layer and the strategy for it. It’s a hands-on, technical role in a fast-moving, greenfield space, so it’s as much strategy as execution.
The opportunity is broad: internal teams (Smart Window, New Products’ automated tools), outside AI tools and their users, and web developers. The three share much of the underlying technology, but each reaches its market in a different way. The mandate is to figure out what to go after, and in what order.

Own the shared foundation and the building blocks it gives other software, and make them reliable and secure.
Push the open standard (WebDriver BiDi) forward, and build Firefox-only advantages the standard won’t cover
Design the safety controls: let a person approve actions, see when software is acting for them, and take back control.
Define the strategy for any major third-party AI assistants people already use.
Serve internal teams (Smart Window, New Products) and outside tools through one shared layer.
Measured on: Adoption across teams and tools, volume of usage through the platform, and sustained reliability and security.

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.
We're looking for a Product Manager to own our search experience that millions of customers land on when they open DoorDash, Wolt, or Deliveroo, and the single biggest lever we have on what they find.
The role sits in our Core Consumer organisation in the Search domain, which is responsible for the in-app experience. You'll be building on a global stack, and your roadmap will be a mix: global platform problems that apply worldwide, global capabilities we're accelerating into EMEA markets, and EMEA-specific problems worth solving properly rather than working around.
Search is where customers tell us exactly what they want. Getting it right across restaurants, grocery, and retail - in every language we operate in - is one of the highest-intent and hardest problems in the app.
What you'll work on
Query understanding, Autosuggestions and AI/ML problems in the Search domain
Where conversational and agentic search changes how customers get to a decision.
Making search work across three brands, multiple languages, and query behaviour that differs market by market.
Our humble expectations
We're looking for a product leader more than a feature owner. Someone who can find the problems that matter most, for customers and for the business, and make the case for solving them.
You bring proven experience as a Product Manager in Consumer, or on another relevance- or ranking-driven consumer experience.
You demonstrate fluency with search measurement and know how to actually move it.
You show strong product judgment, backed by data literacy and customer insight.
You work backwards from the customer problem, and you can weigh that against the most urgent business problems at the same time, rather than treating it as a side you have to pick.
You think strategically: you can zoom out to where the domain should be in two years, then zoom back in on what we should ship next quarter.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely flexible. This industry is changing fast, AI most of all, and the plan we write in January won't be the plan in June.
You work deeply with ML and engineering on relevance and ranking, without needing to be an ML expert yourself.
You're curious about what AI actually changes for customers, and you can tell real value from hype.
You build a case and bring people with you: engineering, design, analytics, and local market teams across three brands and many markets.
You do your best work with range: global platform thinking one week, a specific market's reality the next.
Next steps
The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

About Teramind
Teramind is a global leader in workforce intelligence, insider risk management, and data loss prevention. Used by thousands of companies across 60+ countries, our platform gives organizations the visibility to protect their people, their data, and their operations. We sit at the intersection of three converging markets - Insider Risk, DLP, and Workforce Analytics - and we are one of the few players that spans all three on a unified behavioral data layer.
The Teramind Endpoint Agent is one of the key differentiators of our platform. It runs on hundreds of thousands of endpoints across Windows, macOS, and Linux, capturing the behavioral signal that powers our detection, DLP enforcement, analytics, and AI. The depth and quality of what the Agent sees is a primary reason customers choose Teramind over the alternatives - and the product leader who owns it plays a pivotal role in the company's success.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the Teramind Endpoint Agent, and the AI Usage Control capabilities built on top of it, end to end.

You will be the single accountable product leader for the roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of the Agent organization - approximately half of Teramind engineering, working across operating systems, low-level platform components, and the server-side telemetry pipeline. This is a pivotal role.

The Agent is one of the strongest competitive moats Teramind has, and the next chapter of the product strategy depends on what we build into it. You are coming in to bring product rigor, customer insight, prioritization discipline, and technical judgment to a team that is capable of shipping world-class endpoint technology.

AI Usage Control is one of the most important things you will build here. Companies have spent twenty years governing what employees do with sensitive data, and they now have a second workforce: AI agents reading files, calling tools, and executing commands on the same machines, with none of the accountability.

Nobody has worked out what supervising them looks like, and much of it never touches the network, so the endpoint is the only place you can see it. You will own that end to end. You will sit alongside other product managers, reporting to the VP of Product. Together, you own Teramind's product surface area.
What You Will Own
The Agent roadmap across all platforms. Windows, macOS, Linux, and the platforms after them. You decide what ships, in what order, and why, balancing customer demand, platform modernization, performance, and security hardening on one prioritized backlog.
The endpoint layer of AI Usage Control . Detecting AI that never touches the network - native desktop clients, IDE-embedded assistants, terminal-based coding agents, AI-native Teramind | Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint browsers, and local models running offline - and capturing the prompts, pastes, uploads, and agent-executed commands that browser and network DLP cannot see.
Translating business vision into engineering reality . You turn signals from executives, sales, customers, competitors and the engineering org into a coherent technical roadmap. You are the interpreter between “we need to detect AI exfiltration” and “here is how we instrument the endpoint to see it.”
Building for the enterprise: bulletproof and undetectable . Enterprise customers expect the Agent to be invisible to end users, resilient against tampering, and reliable in conditions that break weaker products. You own the roadmap that keeps it that way.
Performance, footprint, and reliability. Every CPU cycle, megabyte and battery percent we consume is felt by the end user and argued about by the customer's IT team. You set and defend the performance bar.
Define, measure, and meet product KPIs. Adoption, rollout velocity, deployment success rate, crash rates, detection coverage, time-to-patch on OS changes. You set the numbers and hold the team and the company to them.
Industry and ecosystem relationships. Microsoft, Apple, the Linux ecosystem, MDM vendors, and the major AV and EDR vendors. You represent Teramind in technical conversations where the agent's architecture is the subject.

5+ years of product management experience , with at least 3 owning a technical platform, SDK, agent, or systems-level product. This is a senior IC seat: influence without headcount.
Technical depth is non-negotiable . You do not need to write C++, but you should reason about Windows architecture, macOS system extensions, and the trade-offs between Endpoint Security and Network Extension frameworks. You can push back credibly in a design review.
You understand how AI actually runs on a computer . A hosted model in a browser tab, a native desktop client, an IDE-embedded assistant, a CLI coding agent, and a local model under Ollama are five different detection problems, and several are invisible to anything watching the network. You know why, and you know what an audit trail for an autonomous agent has to capture.
Endpoint or systems background. You have shipped endpoint security (EDR, EPP, XDR), monitoring or management agents, OS-level tools, or systems software. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender, Tanium and similar are directly relevant. Pure SaaS and application PMs without systems exposure will struggle here.
You think in outcomes, not features. Success is “95% of customers roll out a new agent version within 30 days,” not “shipped version 27.0.”
You are comfortable with security trade-offs. Visibility versus privacy, tamper protection versus usability, cloud processing versus on-device intelligence. You can hold the attacker's perspective and the IT buyer's perspective in the same conversation.
You work with AI, not just about it. You use AI in your own practice, prototyping to pressure-test concepts before spending engineering cycles, and evaluating model behavior rather than trusting vendor claims.
You bring rigor, and you write. PRDs, decision memos, prioritization frameworks, release cadence, credible engineering-facing specs. In a distributed team, writing is how product management scales.

Engineering background earlier in your career: systems, kernel, driver, or low-level platform work
Windows Filter Drivers, Minifilters or WFP; macOS Endpoint Security or Network Extensions; Linux eBPF, kernel modules or userspace agents
MDM ecosystems (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, Kandji)
Insider risk, DLP, or behavioral analytics
Local model runtimes and on-device inference (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp)
Agentic AI: tool calling, MCP, and autonomous coding or workflow agents
AI governance, AI security, or shadow AI discovery products
EDR and AV co-existence and exclusion lists at scale
Why This Role
Endpoint agents are having a moment. The convergence of insider risk, DLP, AI, and hybrid work is making the endpoint the most strategically important surface in enterprise security and workforce intelligence. Teramind's Agent is one of the deepest data-collection engines in the market - we see things the rest of the category does not - and it is one of the strongest competitive moats we have.

The best of AI at the service of healthcare

Yann LeCun, Meta's Chief AI Scientist and Turing award winner, is an advisor to Nabla.
Product at Nabla
Product development at Nabla is led jointly by Engineering and Product and organized into cross-functional squads. As a Product Manager in the ambient speech-to-text squad, you will join a team focused on speech and ambient intelligence, contributing end-to-end to the evolution of our real-time clinical audio stack.
Your Team
As a Product Manager on the Ambient Speech team, you will own the product strategy and execution for the voice intelligence layer at the heart of Nabla's AI assistant. Ambient speech is the foundation of the clinician experience: it determines what Nabla can reliably hear, understand, and turn into useful documentation and downstream actions.
You will work in a cross-functional squad alongside ML engineers, software engineers, designers, data scientists, and clinical experts. Together, you will turn complex speech and audio capabilities — including transcription, speaker diarization, language detection, and real-time processing — into products that clinicians trust and use every day.

Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Nabla's ambient speech and voice intelligence capabilities
Develop a deep understanding of how clinicians use Nabla in real patient encounters, including the moments where audio quality, speaker attribution, latency, or transcription accuracy affect trust and adoption
Translate clinician needs and business priorities into clear product opportunities, requirements, and success metrics for the speech squad
Partner closely with ML engineers to define the highest-impact improvements across speech recognition, diarization, voice activity detection, principal-speaker detection, language detection, custom vocabulary, and real-time audio processing
Make thoughtful product trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost, reliability, and time to market
Define and monitor product quality metrics that connect technical speech performance with clinician outcomes — such as perceived transcription quality, note quality, edit rates, successful capture rates, activation, retention, and support burden
Lead discovery efforts with clinicians, customers, and internal stakeholders to identify unmet needs across specialties, languages, modalities, and care settings
Design experiments and launch plans that validate new capabilities quickly while protecting the quality and reliability of the core clinical experience
Work with Design to create simple, intuitive experiences that make sophisticated speech technology feel seamless and trustworthy
Collaborate with platform, infrastructure, privacy, security, and downstream product teams to ensure ambient speech capabilities integrate reliably into note generation and future agentic workflows
Build alignment across Product, Engineering, Clinical, Go-to-Market, and leadership teams around priorities, progress, risks, and product decisions
Establish a strong feedback loop from production usage, customer feedback, and operational signals into the squad's roadmap and continuous improvement process
Your DNA
5+ years of technical product management experience, ideally building technical or workflow-critical products
Experience building products powered by machine learning models or working closely with ML teams
Strong product judgment and a demonstrated ability to identify high-value user problems, define a product strategy, and ship meaningful improvements
Experience working closely with engineers and comfort discussing technical systems, data quality, experimentation, APIs, latency, reliability, and product instrumentation
Exceptional ability to translate complex technical capabilities into clear user value, product requirements, and prioritization decisions
Strong analytical skills, including experience defining success metrics, interpreting product data, and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions
A user-obsessed mindset and strong empathy for clinicians operating in high-pressure environments
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create alignment across technical and non-technical stakeholders
Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment with incomplete information, competing priorities, and high ownership

Life at Nabla

## **So sieht dein Alltag aus** ##
* Zum Herzstück: Als Product Owner verantwortest du die Website css.ch und steuerst ihre Weiterentwicklung entlang der Unternehmens- und Digitalstrategie.
* Gemeinsam mit dem Product Management entwickelst du die Produktvision und erarbeitest mit deinem Team Lösungen zur kontinuierlichen Optimierung der Plattform.
* Kundenbedürfnisse und Business-Anforderungen übersetzt du in klare User Stories und Anforderungen für das Entwicklungsteam, pflegst den Backlog und setzt transparente Prioritäten.
* Die technische und inhaltliche Qualität der Website behältst du stets im Blick, insbesondere im Zusammenspiel mit dem Content-Management-System.
* In SAFe-Events bringst du deine Themen aktiv ein, stärkst die Zusammenarbeit im ART und nutzt dein Interesse an neuen Technologien und Künstlicher Intelligenz, um Potenziale für die Plattform zu erkennen.
## **Das bringst du mit** ##
* Das Wichtigste zuerst: Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Rolle als Product Owner oder einer ähnlichen Rolle in agilen Umgebungen und du hast bereits technische Produkte betreut.
* Ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz sowie eine überzeugende und adressatengerechte Kommunikation zeichnen dich aus.
* Dank deiner starken analytischen Fähigkeiten arbeitest du dich rasch in komplexe fachliche und technische Zusammenhänge ein.
* Im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Persönlichkeiten trittst du sicher und empathisch auf und findest auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen tragfähige Lösungen.
* Du verfügst über Erfahrung im Web-Umfeld und bringst ausgewiesene Kenntnisse im Bereich User Experience mit.
